newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil weakens under pressure of softer future.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil weakens under pressure of softer future.

text.p: NWE gas oil was softer on Wednesday as IPE futures fell. Premiums held steady and diesel had to share centre stage as interest for and FOD and DIN grew.
May IPE gas oil closed $2.50 a tonne easier at $162.50 having been knocked lower by bearish APIs.
Traders said diesel interest was still good, but not as much was traded as on Tuesday. A cargo was sold at May IPE +$11.50 basis Le Havre for 20-30 dates.
Barges were pegged around IPE +$10 fob ARA. Supplies of 0.05 percent material were tight on prompt dates and most dealers did not expect a surfeit of material in May.
FOD and DIN interest was stronger on Wednesday with a DIN cargo selling at May IPE +$4.25 cif Germany for 20-30 dates.
A trader was understood to be interested in picking up some FOD at May IPE +$4.50 cif NWE and being met with offers of May IPE +$5.50.
Russian gas oil was still being drawn eastwards leaving little available for NWE. Traders said premiums were around May IPE +$1.50 cif ARA.
